metadata.note: Little Kanawha Railroad, South Parkersburg - Elizabeth - Owensport, WV (~30 mi, Wood and Wirt counties), built 1897-98 as the first leg of a projected Parkersburg - Burnsville coal road and later part of George Gould's Wabash West Virginia scheme; the extensions beyond Palestine/Sandy Bend were graded 1902-03 but never railed and are not drawn (nor is the steamboat route to Creston, which some 1908 press reports counted in the line's length). Two features share identical geometry, split at the 1 May 1908 operator change (CLAUDE.md Rule 4): Little Kanawha Railroad 1902-1908 and Baltimore and Ohio 1908-1915. Built from research/branches/little_kanawha_railroad.txt (2026-10-27).
sources: Parkersburg News and Sentinel 15 Jun 2019 (1897-98 reprints, station list): https://www.newsandsentinel.com/opinion/local-columns/2019/06/look-back-little-kanawha-railroad-a-vital-mid-ohio-valley-artery/
Hur Herald (29.377 mi; extension never railed): http://www.hurherald.com/cgi-bin/db_scripts/articles?Action=user_view&db=hurheral_articles&id=27657
not_yet_sourced: PASSENGER END of the B&O Little Kanawha Branch: drawn to 1915, the last confirmed year [OPEN]. True end unknown, somewhere 1915-1933. Would be settled by the 1930 Official Guide 'Little Kanawha Branch' table (seen only as a caption on American-Rails), the ICC abandonment decisions 193 ICC 559 (1933) and 221 ICC 289 (1937), or ICC Senate Doc. 12, 64th Cong. 1st sess. (1915), pp. 560-649.

PASSENGER START: line opened c. March 1898 but the earliest confirmed passenger evidence is the 1902 Official Guide (via Fowler); 1898-1901 not drawn. Fowler's legend also cites an 1897 company timetable ('z: 1897t'), which predates the opening and is unexplained.

TERMINUS: Palestine (milepost 29.7) vs Owensport (30.2). PRR chronology gives 'Palestine (Owensport)' for 1898 and an opening 'between Parkersburg and Owensport' in Feb 1907; the last ~0.5 mi may not have existed before 1907. Drawn to Owensport for every year.
FREQUENCY: no train count found for any year; headway_min 720 on both segments is an estimate. avg_speed_kmh 32 likewise.

SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: Webster Echo 1908 gives the line as Parkersburg - Creston, 'about fifty miles'; every other source gives ~29.4-31 mi to Palestine/Owensport. Creston was reached only by steamboat; the 50 mi figure is not used.

GEOMETRY: the river crossing between the west-bank South Parkersburg stub and the east-bank Elizabeth - Owensport grade is not located; the ~23.8 mi middle is a river-centreline approximation (see geometry_quality).
metadata.geometry_quality_summary: 7.1 of 31.1 mi real OSM grade/track; 24.0 mi approximated along the river; no straight-line legs.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 31.1 mi (South Parkersburg - Owensport) against a documented 29.377 mi South Parkersburg - Owensport [Hur Herald] / 30.2 mi from Parkersburg Fifth Street [Fowler] / 29.61 mi abandoned 1933+1937 [ICC]; about 3-6% long. Real OSM geometry, 7.1 mi: (1) South Parkersburg - near Stewarts, 3.3 mi, OSM way 15672330 'Little Kanawha Industrial Track' (live CSX/Little Kanawha River Railroad freight track, used as geometry only) and way 168662000 'Little Kanawha Railroad' (railway=abandoned), both tagged note:old_railway_operator=Little Kanawha Railroad; (2) Elizabeth - Palestine - Owensport, 3.8 mi, OSM ways 15667697 (Depot Street), 15667824 (School View) and 168899616 'Little Kanawha Railroad' (railway=abandoned, same tag), chained verbatim. APPROXIMATED, 24.0 mi: near Stewarts - Nicolette - Creels - Kanawha - Cool Spring - Slate - Hughes River - Newark - Sandy Bend - Standing Stone - Elizabeth is drawn along the CENTRELINE OF THE LITTLE KANAWHA RIVER (OSM waterway ways, 23.6 mi) plus two short joins of 858 ft and 927 ft from the river to the mapped grade. It is not a trace of the railroad: the grade was lifted after the 1933/1937 abandonments and no abandoned railway, rail-trail or OpenHistoricalMap way for it exists in this stretch (OHM has only the B&O Parkersburg Branch on the north bank). River-following was chosen over road-following because the railroad hugged the river: measured along the river from the end of the mapped stub, Fowler's mileposts fit within ~0.6 mi at every station (Nicolette 6.1 vs 5.6, Creels 7.3 vs 6.7, Kanawha 9.5 vs 9.6, Cool Spring 12.9 vs 12.3, Slate 15.0 vs 14.5, Hughes River 17.8 vs 17.0, Newark 19.2 vs 18.7, Elizabeth 27.4 vs 26.5); an opstrace road route over WV-14 / county roads instead wandered inland via Mineral Wells and needed a 3.0 mi straight line at Slate, so it was rejected. The approximation cannot show which bank the line used: the mapped grade is on the west (left) bank at South Parkersburg but on the east/north (right) bank at Elizabeth and Palestine, so the railroad crossed the river somewhere in the approximated stretch at a point not identified; the river line also follows every bend where the railroad may have cut across necks, which is most of the ~1 mi excess. No straight-line legs. The drawn line keeps 0 vertices within 50 m of the B&O Parkersburg Branch / North Bend Rail Trail on the north bank. Station distances from the drawn line: Nicolette 0.3 km, Creels 0.3, Kanawha 0.5, Cool Springs 0.8, Slate 0.1, Hughes River mouth 0.0, Newark 0.3, Elizabeth 0.1, Palestine 0.3, Owensport 0.3 km. Starts at the west end of the mapped LK track on the South Parkersburg waterfront; does not cross the Little Kanawha to downtown Parkersburg (passengers crossed by ferry until 1913, then by P.M.&I. interurban). The South Parkersburg stub geometry is the surviving freight track, assumed to sit on the original alignment; not otherwise verified. Draws to Owensport for all years although the last ~0.5 mi Palestine - Owensport may date only from Feb 1907.

segments.note: Little Kanawha Railroad under its own management, South Parkersburg - Elizabeth - Palestine/Owensport, WV (south side of Parkersburg; passengers crossed to downtown by ferry from the wharfboat). START 1902 IS THE EARLIEST CONFIRMED PASSENGER YEAR, NOT THE OPENING [OPEN start]: Fowler's West Virginia passenger-station table 25 lists former station names 'Sheffield 1902G' and 'Stewarts 1902G' from the 1902 Official Guide. The line opened c. March 1898 (PRR chronology 1898; first paid freight to Elizabeth March 1898) and very probably carried passengers from then, but no 1898-1901 source says so in so many words - do not move the start earlier without evidence. END: the company ran its own trains until 30 April 1908; 'commencing May 1' 1908 the Baltimore & Ohio operated the line 'in connection with its own service' (Webster Echo, 1 May 1908, p.4; negotiations reported Evening Journal 5 Dec 1907). The stock-control changes of 1900 (Cartwright/Braxton Coal), c.1901-02 (Gould/Wabash syndicate) and c.1905-07 (P&LE/PRR/B&O community of interest) did not change who ran the trains. headway_min 720 (~one round trip a day) is an UNSOURCED ESTIMATE: no frequency figure was found for any year.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, West Virginia Railroads, table 25 'Little Kanawha RR (BO)' (1902 Official Guide station names) for the start; Webster Echo (Addison WV) 1 May 1908 p.4 for the operator change to the B&O on 1 May 1908; PRR General Chronology 1898 for the March 1898 opening (not used as the start). Frequency NOT SOURCED.

segments.note: Baltimore & Ohio operation of the Little Kanawha Railroad from 1 May 1908 (Webster Echo, 1 May 1908 p.4), the B&O 'Little Kanawha Branch'. Passenger evidence: 'the regular Little Kanawha passenger trains' and a new South Side passenger station for transfer to P.M.&I. interurban cars from downtown Parkersburg (Calhoun Chronicle, 24 June 1913 p.3); the ICC investigation found the road held for 'the transportation of passengers and property', Parkersburg to Owensport, operated at a loss since 1906 and for sale (Mountain State Patriot, 22 Dec 1915 p.2). END 1915 IS THE LAST CONFIRMED PASSENGER YEAR, NOT A KNOWN END [OPEN]: no source dates the last passenger train. Service may have continued into the 1920s (a 1930 Official Guide 'Little Kanawha Branch' table is reported secondhand by American-Rails, contents unseen), but 1933 is the ABANDONMENT of Placid - Owensport (ICC Docket 9875, 20.98 mi) and 1937 of Parkersburg - Placid (Docket 11594, 8.63 mi), not a passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. After abandonment a South Parkersburg stub survived as freight-only track (today's Little Kanawha River Railroad) - not drawn. The B&O's outright purchase (1920 per American-Rails, 'during the 1930s' per WVNC Rails) did not change the operator. headway_min 720 (~one round trip a day) is an UNSOURCED ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Webster Echo 1 May 1908 p.4 (start, B&O operation); Calhoun Chronicle 24 June 1913 p.3 (regular passenger trains, 1913); Mountain State Patriot 22 Dec 1915 p.2 (ICC: passengers and property, 1915 - last confirmed year); Abandoned Rails, ICC dockets 9875 (1933) and 11594 (1937) for the abandonments that bound the unknown end. Frequency NOT SOURCED.
